summary: A table of records with a toolbar, selection, and the three states everyone forgets.
useWhen: showing a list of records the user filters, sorts, selects or acts on in bulk
the row count is unknown at design time — which is what makes the empty and loading states mandatory rather than optional
structure: A toolbar above the table: a search Input, filter controls, and the bulk-action Buttons that appear once something is selected.

Under the toolbar, once any filter is applied: a TagGroup of the active filters, each removable on its own, beside a Clear all Button. When the last one goes the row goes with it, so move focus to the search Input.
Table with a TableHead whose first cell carries the select-all Checkbox, and a TableBody whose rows each carry their own.
Sortable columns: every header that sorts gets `sortDirection` — the current direction on the sorted column, `none` on the others — so each shows it can be sorted before anyone tries.
One region below the table for pagination or a load-more Button.
The table region is replaced — not overlaid — by the empty, loading and error states.

drivenBy.note: It holds which column the rows are sorted by and which way, and `sortProps(column)` gives each sortable header TableCell its `sortDirection` and `onSort`. Choosing a new column sorts it in its `firstDirection` (ascending unless set — pass `descending` for dates and amounts); choosing it again reverses it. It does not reorder rows: sort them yourself from `sort`, or send it to the server when the table is paged. Only the sorted column gets `aria-sort`.

loading.must: Render the table's header row and a fixed number of skeleton rows, keeping the column widths.
loading.why: swapping the whole region for a spinner collapses the layout and moves every control on the page when the data lands
loading.a11y: put `aria-busy="true"` on the container and announce the result count in a live region once it resolves

empty.must: Say which of the two empties this is: no records exist yet, or the current filters match nothing. Offer the action that resolves it — create the first record, or clear the filters.
empty.why: "No results" with no way forward is the single most common dead end in enterprise SaaS, and the two cases need opposite actions
empty.a11y: the empty state carries the heading; do not leave the region unnamed

error.must: Keep the toolbar usable, show an `Alert` with `intent="error"` naming what failed, and offer a retry.
error.why: replacing the whole screen with an error throws away the user's filters and selection, so retrying means rebuilding the query by hand
error.a11y: Alert picks `role="alert"` from the intent — do not add your own

partial.must: When some rows load and others fail, show the rows you have and an Alert above them for the rest.
partial.why: hiding successful rows because a sibling request failed is data loss the user cannot see

requires: `aria-label` on Table — it names the scroll region, which is keyboard reachable
an `aria-label` on every row-selection Checkbox, and `isIndeterminate` on the select-all when the selection is partial
a live region announcing the row count after a filter or search changes it — otherwise a screen-reader user has no idea the table changed
a sortable header's label is its accessible name — the button inside the <th> reads the column name, and `aria-sort` on the sorted <th> says the direction
notes: Bulk-action Buttons appearing on selection is a change of available actions, not just of styling. Announce it.

antiPatterns.dont: a spinner replacing the whole table region
antiPatterns.do: skeleton rows under the real header
antiPatterns.why: the layout collapses and every control below the table jumps when data arrives

antiPatterns.dont: one empty state for both "nothing exists" and "nothing matches"
antiPatterns.why: the resolving action is opposite in each case — create something, or clear the filter

antiPatterns.do: a Link or Button inside a cell
antiPatterns.why: a row takes no focus, so a keyboard user can never fire it, and an interactive role on <tr> is not valid HTML

antiPatterns.dont: destructive bulk actions with no confirmation
antiPatterns.why: select-all plus delete is one click away from removing everything the filter matched

antiPatterns.dont: wrapping Table in your own scroll container
antiPatterns.why: Table already owns one and makes it keyboard reachable; a second is unreachable

antiPatterns.dont: a sortable column with no indicator until it is clicked
antiPatterns.do: `sortDirection="none"` on every sortable header, so the neutral arrows show which columns sort
antiPatterns.why: a header that sorts but looks like plain text is only found by accident

antiPatterns.dont: sorting only the current page of a paged table
antiPatterns.why: the reader sees "A–Z" and takes it as the whole list; send the sort to the server, which knows every row
